main.claim: Open this speaker test, choose left, right or both, and hear a tone come from the side you picked. Use the frequency slider or the sweep to check more of the range. Free, in your browser, no sign-up.

sections.heading: How to test your speakers
sections.body:
Start at a low volume, because a tone can be louder than you expect. Then check the sides one at a time, so you know which speaker is playing.

1. Open [Speaker Test](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/).
2. Set the volume slider low, then raise it until the tone is comfortable.
3. Choose left. The tone should come only from the left speaker, and the left indicator lights up while it plays.
4. Choose right, then both. The right indicator should light up, and both speakers should play together.
5. Move the frequency slider to hear tones from 100 to 2000 Hz. Press the sweep to run through that whole range in one go.

**Listen for the side, not just the sound.** A tone on the wrong side means your channels are swapped. A tone that plays on no side means the speaker or the output setting needs a check.

sections.heading: When you hear nothing
sections.body:
Check the easy things first. Raise the volume on your speakers and on your computer, make sure nothing is muted, and confirm the speakers are the output your computer is using. Headphones or a headset that are still plugged in can take over the sound, so unplug them before you test the speakers.

If you still hear nothing, the cause is usually the output setting, the cable or the speaker itself. Try the same test with headphones. If headphones work and the speakers do not, check the speakers, their cable and their power.

sections.heading: Find the page for your device
sections.body:
The steps differ by device, so use the page that matches yours:

- [Speaker test for laptop](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/laptop) for built-in laptop speakers and Windows output settings.
- [Speaker test for PC](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/pc) for desktop speakers.
- [Speaker test for Zoom](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/zoom) to run Zoom's own speaker test next to this one.
- [Speaker test on iPhone](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/iphone) for Apple's sound checks.

If you are checking which side each speaker plays, read the [left and right test](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/left-right).

sections.heading: What this tool does not check
sections.body:
This test plays tones only. It does not record anything, and it does not judge how music or speech sounds. A clean tone on each side tells you the speakers get sound and play it on the right channel. To hear how real audio sounds, play a song you know well after the test.

To check a microphone, use the [mic test](https://mic-test.lazur.app/).

pages.title: Speaker Test iPhone: Check Your Sound in Safari | Lazur
pages.description: Check your iPhone speakers in Safari with a free speaker test: left, right and both tones, plus a sweep. If nothing plays, Apple's steps help. No app needed.
pages.claim: Open the speaker test in Safari on your iPhone, turn off Silent mode, and play a tone. Choose left, right or both to hear each side. If nothing plays, Apple's steps below check the speaker, the slider and your settings. Free, no app.

sections.heading: Check the iPhone speaker in Safari
sections.body:
Start with Silent mode. Apple's first check is to make sure the Ring/Silent switch is set so no orange shows.

1. Move the Ring/Silent switch so no orange shows.
2. Take off any case or screen protector that covers the speaker opening.
3. Open [Speaker Test](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/iphone) in Safari.
4. Set the volume slider low, then raise it until the tone is comfortable.
5. Choose left, then right, then both. Watch the matching indicator light up while each tone plays.

If the tone is clear and steady, the phone is sending sound out in Safari. Hold the phone the way you normally do, because a hand over the speaker can muffle the sound.

sections.heading: If you hear nothing
sections.body:
Apple's steps are a good next check. Work through them in order.

- Turn off Do Not Disturb. Apple's path is Settings, then Focus, then Do Not Disturb.
- Clean the speaker opening with a small, soft, dry brush. Do not push anything into it.
- Drag the Ringtone and Alerts slider in Settings, under Sounds or Sounds & Haptics, back and forth a few times. You should hear a sound as it moves.

If the slider gives no sound, or its speaker button looks dimmed, Apple says the speaker may need service. Apple's full page is [If you hear no sound or distorted sound from your iPhone, iPad, or iPod touch speaker](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118432).

sections.heading: Check calls separately
sections.body:
The speaker test plays sound through Safari. It does not show whether the earpiece works for calls. To check that, place a call with speakerphone on and listen for the other person.

Apple says that if you hear static or crackling on a call, reception may be the problem. Try again later or from another place before you decide the speaker is broken.

Run the speaker test a second time after each change, with the same volume setting. That way a difference in the result comes from the change you made, not from a louder or quieter tone. If you contact Apple or a repair shop, write down the steps you already tried, so you do not have to repeat them.

sections.heading: Left and right on iPhone
sections.body:
Left and right only show a difference if the device has stereo output. Test the both option first. If it is clear and steady, then listen to left and right on their own. If both sides sound the same to you, that is how the device plays, not a fault in the test.

If you use earbuds or headphones with your iPhone, run the same test with them connected, then compare the result with the phone's own sound. A tone that is clear in one and quiet in the other points to the device you are wearing, not to the phone.

faq.q: How do I check if my iPhone speakers are working?
faq.a: Turn off Silent mode, open the speaker test in Safari, and play the both option at a low volume. A clear, steady tone means sound is coming out of the phone. If you hear nothing, work through Apple's Ringtone and Alerts slider check in Settings.

faq.q: How do I run a speaker diagnostic on iPhone?
faq.a: This tool does not run a diagnostic on the phone. For a quick check, drag the Ringtone and Alerts slider in Settings, under Sounds or Sounds & Haptics, and listen. If you hear nothing, or the speaker button is dimmed, Apple says the speaker may need service.

faq.q: How do I test my audio on iPhone?
faq.a: Open the speaker test in Safari, set the volume low, then play left, right, both and the sweep from 100 to 2000 Hz. Listen for even volume, clear tones and any crackle. For calls, make a test call with speakerphone on.

faq.q: How do I test if my phone speaker is working?
faq.a: Play the both option in the speaker test and listen for a clear tone. If there is no sound, turn off Silent mode, clean the speaker opening, and check the Ringtone and Alerts slider. The test covers sound output in Safari, not the earpiece for calls.

pages.title: Speaker Test Left Right: Check Each Side Free | Lazur
pages.description: Play a tone through the left speaker only, then the right only, and find out if your stereo channels are swapped or silent. Free, in your browser.
pages.claim: Choose left and listen: the tone should come only from the left speaker. Then choose right. If the left tone plays on the right side, your channels are swapped. Free, in your browser, no sign-up.

sections.heading: How to check left and right
sections.body:
Use the same order every time, so you can tell a fault from a setting.

1. Open [Speaker Test](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/left-right).
2. Set the volume slider low.
3. Choose left. Listen for the tone and check that the left indicator lights up.
4. Choose right. The tone should come from the right speaker, and the right indicator lights up.
5. Choose both. You should hear the same tone from both sides at the same level.

**Judge by the side you hear, not the light.** The indicator shows what the tool is sending. Your ears show what the speakers are doing.

sections.heading: What the result means
sections.body:
- **Left plays left and right plays right:** the channels are correct.
- **Left plays right, or right plays left:** the channels are swapped. Switch the speakers or their connections, then test again.
- **One side is silent:** check that both speakers have power and that the cable is fully pushed in. Some speaker sets have a link between the two speakers, so check that link too.
- **Both sides are quiet:** raise the volume on the speakers and on your computer, then check the balance control in your sound settings. A balance pushed to one side makes that side quieter.
- **Nothing plays at all:** see the steps on the [speaker test home page](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/).

After any change, run left, right and both again from the start.

If you use a sound bar, a monitor or a set of desktop speakers with a left and right side, work through the same order for each one. Note which cable goes where before you move anything, so you can put it back if the result gets worse.

sections.heading: Headphones and earbuds
sections.body:
Headphones and earbuds use the same test. Put them on the right way: the left cup or bud is marked L, and the right is marked R. If the sides sound swapped in headphones, check the marking and how you are wearing them first.

If only one earbud plays, check that it is fully seated and charged, then test again. Headphones are a quick way to tell whether a problem is in one speaker or in the connection.

sections.heading: Use the sweep when a side sounds wrong
sections.body:
The sweep plays tones that move from 100 Hz to 2000 Hz. Low tones sound deep and high tones sound sharper. Run the sweep on the side that sounds wrong, then on the other side, and compare.

A side that buzzes, rattles or cuts out at certain pitches can point to a loose or damaged speaker. A side that stays clear at every pitch is working. This test checks which side plays and how the tones sound. It does not measure sound quality.

faq.q: How do I know if my speakers are left and right?
faq.a: Choose left in the speaker test and listen. If the tone comes from the left speaker, that side is correct. Then do the same with right. Finish with both to check that the two sides match in volume.

faq.q: What if the left speaker plays on the right side?
faq.a: Your channels are swapped. Switch the connections or the speakers, so the speaker you want on the left is on the left, then run the left and right test again. The test shows the result, but it does not change any setting on your computer.

faq.q: Why does only one of my speakers play?
faq.a: Usually the cause is a cable, a power switch or a link between two speakers. Check that both speakers are on and that the cable is fully pushed in, then test again. If the silent side still does not play, try that speaker on another device.

pages.title: Speaker Test for Laptop: Check Your Speakers Free | Lazur
pages.description: Test your laptop speakers in the browser with left, right and both tones, plus a sweep. If nothing plays, check the output in Windows 11 Settings. Free.
pages.claim: Open the speaker test on your laptop, set the volume low, and choose left, right or both to hear the tone from the built-in speakers. If nothing plays, check the output device in Windows 11 Settings. Free, no sign-up.

sections.heading: Test the laptop speakers
sections.body:
Set the laptop volume to a middle level before you start, so the tone is easy to hear without being loud.

1. Unplug headphones, a headset or any dock with audio, so the tone goes to the laptop speakers.
2. Open [Speaker Test](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/laptop).
3. Set the volume slider low, then raise it until the tone is comfortable.
4. Choose both. Listen for a clear tone with no buzz.
5. Choose left, then right. Each tone should come from its own side.
6. Run the sweep from 100 to 2000 Hz and listen for crackle or rattling.

**Small speakers struggle with the lowest tones.** The bottom of the sweep may sound thin on a laptop. That is normal for speakers this size, not a fault.

Test the laptop in the same place you normally work. A laptop on a soft surface, such as a bed or a sofa cushion, can muffle the sound, so the tone may seem quieter than it is. Lift the laptop onto a desk and test again before you decide the speakers are weak.

sections.heading: Check the output in Windows 11
sections.body:
If you hear nothing, or the tone plays on the wrong device, check the output in Windows. Microsoft's steps are:

1. Select Start, then Settings, then System, then Sound.
2. In the Output section, select the device you want, such as your speakers.
3. Run the speaker test again.

Selecting a device in Output also makes it the default. If you have more than one output, such as a laptop speaker and a docking station or Bluetooth speaker, only the one selected in Output will play the tone. Choose the device you want to test, then run the test again. To change the volume, select the speaker icon on the taskbar, then the arrow to the right of the speaker volume slider to see your devices. Microsoft's guide is [Fix sound or audio problems in Windows](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/audio/fix-sound-or-audio-problems-in-windows).

sections.heading: Check the volume mixer
sections.body: One app can be muted or turned down while the rest of Windows plays. Select the settings icon to the right of the Volume mixer slider to open the mixer. Make sure none of the controls are muted. If one is, select the Unmute speakers icon. Some speakers and apps have their own volume controls, so check those too.

sections.heading: Run the Windows audio troubleshooter
sections.body:
If the tone plays here but Windows shows no output, run the audio troubleshooter:

1. Select Start, then Settings, then System.
2. Select Troubleshoot, then Other troubleshooters.
3. In the Audio section, select Run.

If the troubleshooter finds a fix, apply it and play the tone again. If nothing changes, the speakers, their cable or their driver may need a check.

faq.q: How do I test if my laptop speakers are working?
faq.a: Open the speaker test, set the volume low, and choose both. A clear tone from the built-in speakers means they work. If you hear nothing, check Output under Settings, System, Sound, and check the volume mixer.

faq.q: How can I test my speaker?
faq.a: Use the speaker test to play tones through each side: left, right, both and the sweep from 100 to 2000 Hz. Start with the volume low. If you hear the tone, the speaker plays. If not, check the output device in Windows and the volume mixer.

faq.q: How to check if audio is working in a laptop?
faq.a: Play the both option in the speaker test. If you hear a steady tone, audio is coming out of the laptop. If you hear nothing, unplug any headphones, check the Output device in Windows Settings, and run the Windows audio troubleshooter.

faq.q: How do I test audio quality?
faq.a: This tool checks that each side plays and how the tones sound. It does not score sound quality. To judge quality, play a song or video you know well at a moderate volume and listen for clear highs, steady bass and no crackle.

pages.title: Speaker Test for Zoom: Check Speakers Before a Call | Lazur
pages.description: Check your speakers for Zoom: run Zoom's Test speaker in Settings, then a free browser tone test with left, right and both. No sign-up needed.
pages.claim: Zoom has its own Test speaker button in Settings, under Audio. Run it, then use this free browser test to play left, right and both tones and confirm your speakers work before you join. No sign-up.

sections.heading: Test speakers in Zoom's settings
sections.body:
Zoom's own test checks the speaker Zoom is set to use. You can run it before you join a meeting, from the desktop app:

1. Open the Zoom desktop app and click your profile picture in the top-right corner.
2. Click Settings.
3. Click the Audio tab.
4. In the Speaker section, click Test speaker. Zoom plays a test tone.
5. If you can't hear it, choose a different speaker from the menu, or adjust Volume.

Zoom's help article is [Testing your audio settings for Zoom meetings](https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0062765).

sections.heading: Test speakers while you join
sections.body:
When you join a meeting, Zoom can run the speaker test for you:

1. Click Test speaker and microphone. A pop-up window opens.
2. If you don't hear the ringtone, use the drop-down menu, or click No, Try Another Speaker, until you do.
3. Click Yes to move on to the microphone test.
4. Click End test.
5. Click Join audio in the meeting controls toolbar.

To switch speakers during a meeting, click the arrow next to Mute or Unmute in the meeting controls toolbar, then choose the speaker you want.

sections.heading: Check the speakers in your browser
sections.body:
Zoom's test checks Zoom's output. Your browser can use a different speaker from the one Zoom picked, so run the browser test as well:

1. Open [Speaker Test](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/zoom).
2. Set the volume slider low.
3. Choose both, then left and right.
4. If the tone comes from the speaker you want Zoom to use, the two match.

**Match the two.** If Zoom's speaker setting and the browser test point at different speakers, change one so both use the same speakers, then run Zoom's test again.

sections.heading: If nothing plays in Zoom
sections.body:
Check the basics first: the volume on the speakers, the computer volume and Zoom's own Volume control. Make sure the speaker selected in Zoom's Audio tab is the one you are listening to, not a headset you have taken off. If the browser tone also plays nothing, the problem is in the computer's output. For Windows 11 output steps, see the [speaker test for laptop](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/laptop) page.

After you change any setting, run Zoom's test once more from the start, so you can hear whether the change took effect before you join.

If Zoom's test passes but you still hear nothing in a meeting, leave the meeting, check that the same speaker is selected in the meeting controls, and join again. Keep the Zoom window open while you test, and do not close it until the tone is clear.

faq.q: How do I test my speakers on Zoom?
faq.a: Open Zoom's Settings from your profile picture, click Audio, then click Test speaker in the Speaker section. If you can't hear the tone, pick another speaker from the menu or adjust the volume. You can run this before you join a meeting.

faq.q: Can I test my Zoom audio without being in a meeting?
faq.a: Yes. Open Settings, click Audio, and use Test speaker. You don't need to join a meeting. The test uses the speaker Zoom has selected, so check that choice before you run it.

faq.q: How do I test my mic and speakers?
faq.a:
Start joining a meeting and click Test speaker and microphone. Zoom plays a tone, then moves on to the microphone test when you click Yes. Use the speaker test here to check left, right and both tones on their own.

If Zoom's test works but a call still sounds quiet on the other end, check the microphone with its own test before the meeting, and make sure Zoom is using the headset or mic you plan to wear.

pages.title: Speaker Test PC: Check Your Desktop Speakers Free | Lazur
pages.description: Test PC speakers in the browser with left, right and both tones, plus a sweep. If you hear nothing, check the output in Windows 11 Settings. Free.
pages.claim: Open the speaker test on your PC, set the volume low, and choose left, right, both or the sweep. If you hear the tone, the speakers work. If not, pick the output in Windows 11 Settings, then test again. Free, no sign-up.

sections.heading: Check the speakers are connected
sections.body:
Before you open the test, check the basics. Turn the speakers on and set their own volume to a middle level. Many desktop speakers plug into the green audio jack on the back of the PC, and a loose plug is a common reason for no sound.

If you use a monitor with built-in speakers or a USB headset, make sure Windows is using that device, as described in the next section.

sections.heading: Test the PC speakers
sections.body:
1. Open [Speaker Test](https://speaker-test.lazur.app/pc).
2. Set the volume slider low, then raise it until the tone is comfortable.
3. Choose both and listen for one steady tone.
4. Choose left, then right. Each tone should come from its own speaker.
5. Run the sweep from 100 to 2000 Hz. Listen for buzzing, rattling or gaps.

If the tone is steady and comes from the right side each time, the speakers and their connection work for this test.

Run the sweep at a low volume first, then raise the volume and run it again. A tone that is clean at a low level but buzzes when louder can point to a speaker that is pushed past its limit, so keep the volume at a level you would use for music.

sections.heading: Set the output in Windows 11
sections.body:
If the tone plays nowhere, or from the wrong device, choose the output in Windows:

1. Select Start, then Settings, then System, then Sound.
2. In the Output section, select the speakers you want.
3. Run the speaker test again.

Selecting a device in Output also makes it the default. Microsoft's guide is [Fix sound or audio problems in Windows](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/audio/fix-sound-or-audio-problems-in-windows).

sections.heading: Check the volume mixer and your apps
sections.body: If the tone plays but a game, video or call app is silent, that app may be muted or turned down. Select the settings icon to the right of the Volume mixer slider, then check that no control is muted. If one is, select the Unmute speakers icon. Some apps also have their own volume control, so check it too.

sections.heading: If Windows does not see your speakers
sections.body:
If your speakers are not listed under Output, Windows cannot see them. Check the cable and the power, then try another port. Then run the audio troubleshooter: select Start, then Settings, then System, then Troubleshoot, then Other troubleshooters. In the Audio section, select Run. If the speakers still do not appear, check the driver for your sound card or motherboard.

If you use a desktop speaker set with a volume knob or a separate power switch, check both before you change any setting in Windows. A knob turned all the way down looks exactly like a broken output, and it takes a few seconds to check.

faq.q: How do I test if a speaker is bad?
faq.a: Play the left, right and sweep tones in the speaker test. A speaker that is quiet on one side, or that buzzes, rattles or cuts out at certain pitches, may be damaged or loose. Check the cable first, then try that speaker on another device if you can.

faq.q: How do I test if my audio is working?
faq.a: Open the speaker test and choose both. A steady tone from your speakers means the PC is sending audio out. If you hear nothing, check the Output section in Windows Settings, the volume mixer and the cable.

faq.q: Why is my PC not detecting speakers?
faq.a: Windows lists only the outputs it can see. Check that the speakers are on and plugged into the right port, then open Settings, System, Sound and look at Output. If the speakers still do not appear, run the Windows audio troubleshooter.
